nodes.label: Container RL Env
nodes.rationale: Simulates the board game Container as an RL environment with JAX acceleration, enabling both human play via TUI and RL agent training. Supports single-player local TUI, multiplayer TCP server, recurrent multi-container actions, MaskablePPO action masking, and persistent SQLite game state.

nodes.label: Game Server Architecture
nodes.rationale: The server owns game state and is authoritative — clients are thin terminals that render the board and send action indices. All game logic runs server-side via env.step(). Game state is persisted to SQLite after every action, supporting disconnection and rejoin. Communication happens over TCP with JSON messages.

nodes.label: SQLite Persistent Game State
nodes.rationale: Game state is persisted to SQLite after every action, enabling players to disconnect and rejoin mid-game using name and password. The database stores both state and player information on the server side.

nodes.label: Client TUI
nodes.rationale: Thin client terminals that render the board state and send action indices to the server. Supports keyboard-driven controls for all game actions including buying, producing, loading ships, auctions, loans, and history browsing.

nodes.label: Recurrent Multi-Container Actions
nodes.rationale: Actions like Produce, BuyFromFactory, and LoadShip support selecting multiple containers in a single turn, requiring recurrent action space handling for RL training.

nodes.label: Contributor Covenant 3.0
nodes.rationale: Adapted from Contributor Covenant 3.0, stewarded by the Organization for Ethical Source and licensed under CC BY-SA 4.0. The enforcement ladder was inspired by Mozilla's code of conduct team.

nodes.label: Code of Conduct Enforcement Ladder
nodes.rationale: Four-tier graduated enforcement: Warning → Temporarily Limited Activities → Temporary Suspension → Permanent Ban. Lower rungs may be skipped for severe violations. Designed to repair harm with escalating consequences based on impact to individuals and community.

nodes.label: Alls-Green Gate Pattern
nodes.rationale: A final CI job that depends on all prior jobs (lint, type-check, test, coverage) and only passes if every dependency succeeded. Used as a single required status check target for branch protection, avoiding the need to update the required-checks list when jobs are added or removed.

nodes.label: SLSA Build Provenance Attestations
nodes.rationale: Generates cryptographically verifiable SLSA provenance attestations for PyPI release artifacts via actions/attest-build-provenance, enabling consumers to verify the build chain integrity of published packages.

nodes.label: PyPI Trusted Publishing
nodes.rationale: Uses OpenID Connect (OIDC) to authenticate GitHub Actions to PyPI without long-lived API tokens. Requires environment protection rules in GitHub Settings with required reviewers and tag-restricted deployment to prevent unauthorized publishes.

nodes.label: AI Provenance Disclosure
nodes.rationale: PR template requires AI-generated contributions to disclose the tool (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, etc.), model, and prompt/thread. This section is meant to be removed for human-authored PRs, establishing a transparency norm for AI-assisted development.

nodes.label: Minimal Workflow Permissions
nodes.rationale: All GitHub Actions workflows use permissions: {} at the top level with per-job scoping, following the principle of least privilege. This prevents token leakage and limits the blast radius of a compromised workflow.

nodes.label: SHA-Pinned GitHub Actions
nodes.rationale: All third-party actions are pinned by full commit SHA with version comments rather than floating tags, preventing supply-chain attacks where a tag is moved to a malicious commit. Complemented by Dependabot for automated SHA updates.

nodes.label: Cache Poisoning Prevention in Release Pipeline
nodes.rationale: Cache is explicitly disabled (enable-cache: false) in the PyPI publish workflow's setup-uv step to prevent cache-poisoning attacks on release artifacts, trading build speed for supply-chain integrity during the release process.

nodes.label: Dependabot 7-Day Cooldown Policy
nodes.rationale: A 7-day cooldown (default-days: 7) between Dependabot update PRs prevents automatically adopting compromised releases immediately, giving the community time to detect and report malicious package versions before they are merged.

nodes.label: ContainerFunctional
nodes.rationale: Pure functional JAX design (jax.jit-compatible transition/observation/reward) enables GPU-accelerated RL training.

nodes.label: ActionEncoder
nodes.rationale: Legacy encoder kept for backward compatibility so existing flat-index code continues to work alongside the new multi-head format.

nodes.label: Multi-Head Action Space
nodes.rationale: Multi-head design chosen over flat index for: (1) generalisation — feedback on colour/price/opponent heads independently improves sample efficiency; (2) per-head action masks zero out invalid options before softmax so the agent never wastes time on illegal actions; (3) recurrent shopping (Option B) allows multiple purchases per action with summed log-probs matching PPO formula.

nodes.label: Recurrent Shopping Mechanism
nodes.rationale: Option B design: actions 3 and 4 can buy multiple containers in a single action (matching real rules). After first purchase, shopping_active=True; training loop calls policy again for each subsequent purchase until STOP or constraints exhausted. Total log-prob for PPO = sum of all sub-step log-probs.

nodes.label: Action Masks
nodes.rationale: Per-head binary masks appended to observation vector so policy can apply masked_logits = logits + log(mask) then softmax, ensuring illegal actions get zero probability.

nodes.label: No-Op + Per-Mode Masking (v3)
nodes.rationale: Every head has no-op at index 0. In parallel mode (normal turn) no-op is masked out and all legal values shown. In sequential mode (shopping/produce continuation) irrelevant heads are forced to no-op; only relevant heads are active. This cleanly separates turn-level and sub-action choices.

nodes.label: Recurrent Produce
nodes.rationale: Produce requires one initial entry step (pay $1 union boss, set produce_active=1) then one sequential step per factory to choose colour + price or leave idle. Turn advances only after all factories processed.

nodes.label: Auction Resolution
nodes.rationale: Auction always ends the acting player's turn, even if it is the first action taken. Seller may accept (collect from winner + bank) or reject (pay bank, keep cargo). This is a high-stakes mechanism central to the game's economy.

nodes.label: Domestic Sale Variant
nodes.rationale: Official beginner's variant recommended by publisher Valley Games for 5-person games. Adds an 8th action allowing a player to return a container to supply for $2, providing a guaranteed income floor.

nodes.label: Interest Payment Errata
nodes.rationale: Official publisher errata from Kevin Nesbitt (game designer) clarifying the bank seizure procedure when a player cannot pay interest. Cascading asset seizure: Island Store → Harbour Store (2:1) → Factory Store (1:1) → Warehouse/Machine.

nodes.label: Bubble Tea TUI
nodes.rationale: Bubble Tea (Charm library) renders the TUI over the PTY channel inside the SSH session. Requires TERM=xterm-256color from the SSH client.

nodes.label: SSH Key-Based Auth Flow
nodes.rationale: SSH key is the sole identity mechanism — no passwords needed. On first connection, key is captured and bound to a username; subsequent connections auto-login. Unknown keys get signup prompt; password-only connections are rejected with instructions to generate a key first.

nodes.label: Port Swap Procedure (OpenSSH ↔ container-rl-ssh)
nodes.rationale: Swap port 22 (OpenSSH) with port 2222 (container-rl-ssh) so users can connect with plain 'ssh hostname' while admin SSH access is preserved on port 2222.
